title: Flank Steak – Stuffed With Italian Filling & Rolled
description:
Impress anyone with this easy flank steak that's rolled with garlic, herbs, prosciutto ham and provolone cheese – these are the ultimate Italian steak pinwheels!
You may have seen a few stuffed flank steak recipes where the rolled “log” is sliced into pinwheels BEFORE cooking – the cook time is shorter, about 8-10+ minutes, or until your steak reaches your desired temperature.
In this one, the entire log is browned for a few minutes on each side, then roasted until you get the desired doneness; finally sliced for presentation. It’s a lot easier and more dramatic this way.
ingredients: 3 - 4 cloves garlic minced or pressed through garlic press
directions: Combine garlic, shallot, parsley, basil, sage, and olive oil in small bowl.
Slicing horizontally across the steak, butterfly and carefully pound the flank steak into 2 thin rectangles.
Position steak so that the grain runs parallel to the edge of the counter, spreading the herb mixture evenly over the surface of the steak.
Lay prosciutto evenly over steak, leaving 1-inch border along top edge.
Cover prosciutto with an even layer of cheese, leaving 1-inch border along top edge.
Starting from bottom edge and rolling up away from you, towards the top. Form the steak roll into a tight log and place on cutting board seam-side down.

Starting in the middle of the steak roll, tie a piece of kitchen twine to secure the steak. Working outward from the center, place more ties of kitchen twine, in one inch or so intervals, until the whole steak roll is tied up.
Heat a cast iron skillet or full-size pan over medium high heat. Then brown the roll on all four sides, about 2 minutes each.
Slide skillet into preheated oven and cook for about 20+ minutes, depending on the thickness, or until steak reaches desired doneness (125 degrees for medium rare).
Remove from oven, tent with aluminum foil, and let rest for 5 minutes.
Remove twine and slice into individual portions.
